title: The Beatles’ Apple Boutique mural is whitewashed | 1968
content:
The psychedelic mural which adorned the exterior of The Beatles’ Apple Boutique was whitewashed from 15-18 May 1968.

The Beatles opened the store on 7 December 1967. It was located at 94 Baker Street, London.

The design company known as The Fool, who were known by The Beatles, were given £100,000 to design and stock the boutique with their garments and accessories, and to decorate the building.

One of The Fool’s designers, Barry Finch, employed several dozen art students to paint a psychedelic mural across the building’s front between 10 and 12 November 1967. Westminster Council had refused them permission but The Fool decided to press on regardless.

Within two weeks of the boutique opening, however, complaints from local traders resulted in the council issuing Apple with an order to repaint the building in its original colour.

On 8 May 1968 a solicitor for the Portman Estate, landowners who had sold the property to The Beatles, told the press: “The property is protected by a covenant to ensure it is kept in the traditions of a ‘high class shopping locality’. The trustees felt that the decorations are a breach of the covenant.”

The Beatles accepted the claim, and agreed to comply with the landlord’s wishes to have the exterior mural painted over. The repainting began on 15 May and was completed three days later.

The change coincided with a souring of relations between The Beatles and The Fool. This day’s edition of the Daily Sketch newspaper reported that the design collective’s five-year contract had been terminated after eight months. The Fool’s Simon Posthuma was quoted as saying: “We are fed up with The Beatles”. In turn, Apple’s managing director Neil Aspinall told the press: “I think they were too far-out for everybody. Mostly though, they wanted to run the whole show.”
